section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section provides the opening header and date for the maamar.
section.t: With the help of Heaven.
Night of the third [day] of Selichos,
the year 5720*

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the two interpretations of "seek My face" in prayer, corresponding to supplication and searching, which are the heart's work within and with the heart.
section.t: "To You my heart said: 'Seek My face' etc."1,
And the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, brings in his maamar beginning with the words "Zeh"2
Rashi's commentary on the verse,
that there are two interpretations in "Lecha" [to you/for you].
For you, in your mission, and in your place.
And he continues in the maamar,
that also in "seek My face" there are two interpretations.
That "seek" is a request and supplication,
and that "seek" is a request and search.
And he explains,
that these two matters
(request and supplication,
request and search)
are in prayer.
For prayer is a request and supplication,
and the request is that he succeed in his service to search and find the ways of correction in all his matters.
And this is what is written: "To You my heart said: 'Seek My face'"
(specifically "my heart"),
because the two matters of "seek My face" are in prayer
(as above),
and prayer is the service of the heart3.
And he adds in the maamar,
that in the service of the heart there are two matters.
Within the heart and with the heart.
And it can be said,
that these two matters correspond to the two interpretations
(above)
in "seek My face."
For the request and supplication in prayer come through the service within the heart,
so that his request and supplication will be true,
it is by arousing his heart,
service in the heart itself.
And the search in prayer
(how to correct all his matters)
is service with the heart.
That is,
the service is
(not in the heart,
but)
in all his matters,
except that this service is through the heart4.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the verse "From my flesh I shall perceive G-d," distinguishing between intellectual and tangible perception, and how human soul-powers derive from the supernal Sefiros.
section.t: B)
And to explain this,
the maamar prefaces with what is written5
"And from my flesh I shall perceive G-d,"
that one must understand: the main thing is the soul, so why does it say "And from my flesh I shall perceive"?
And he explains,
that in perception there are two modes,
intellectual perception and tangible perception.
For intellectual perception relates more to the soul,
and tangible perception relates more to the body.
And this distinction is also regarding the thing perceived.
For in every thing there is a body and a soul.
For even in physical things there is the soul within them6,
and even in spiritual things there is the body within them.
And therefore it says "And from my flesh I shall perceive G-d,"
because the intent of "I shall perceive G-d" is for tangible perception in G-dliness,
for there are matters of G-dliness,
such as Divine Providence,
that one can perceive tangibly.
And he continues in the maamar7
in the explanation of the verse "And from my flesh I shall perceive G-d,"
that the powers of the human soul descend from the supernal Sefiros8
as it is written9
"Let us make man in our image, after our likeness,"
and therefore,
from the powers of the human soul one can understand the supernal Sefiros.
